expectedText:
IAEA NOTICE OF PROPOSED ACTION PROCEDURE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Pat Morgan · Morgan Lee

PURPOSE OF THIS REFERENCE — NOTICE OF PROPOSED ACTION PROCEDURE
This document describes, as general information, the notice-of-proposed-action procedure set out in Probate Code §§ 10580-10592 — the mechanism that lets a personal representative who has Independent Administration of Estates Act (IAEA) authority take many actions in administering the estate of Pat Morgan by giving written notice to interested persons, rather than by filing a separate court petition for each action. Morgan Lee is identified here as the personal representative (or proposed personal representative) of Pat Morgan's estate to whom this reference applies. This document does not itself propose, describe, or give notice of any specific action regarding Pat Morgan's estate; it does not draft, serve, or file any actual Notice of Proposed Action, objection, waiver, consent, or restraining order; and it does not determine whether any particular action available to Morgan Lee requires this procedure, is exempt from it, or has already been waived or consented to by a given interested person. This document is background information for that separate process, not a substitute for it, and not itself a notice, objection, waiver, or consent with legal effect.

WHEN A PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVE MUST GIVE NOTICE OF PROPOSED ACTION, AND WHEN GIVING IT IS OPTIONAL
The notice-of-proposed-action procedure does not apply to every action a personal representative with IAEA authority might take regarding Pat Morgan's estate. Probate Code § 10580(a) requires a personal representative who has IAEA authority to give notice of proposed action under this chapter before taking a proposed action without court supervision only if the specific provision of Chapter 3 (Probate Code §§ 10500 et seq.) that grants the power to take that action itself requires notice to be given; § 10580(a) also makes clear that this chapter does not by itself authorize a personal representative to take any action the personal representative does not otherwise have power to take under Part 6. Separately, § 10580(b) permits a personal representative to give notice of proposed action voluntarily even for an action that Chapter 3 permits to be taken without notice — but doing so for one action does not create a notice obligation for other actions where § 10580(a) does not require it, and does not expand the personal representative's underlying authority.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "10580. (a) A personal representative who has been granted authority to administer the estate under this part shall give notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter prior to the taking of the proposed action without court supervision if the provision of Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 10500) giving the personal representative the power to take the action so requires. Nothing in this subdivision authorizes a personal representative to take an action under this part if the personal representative does not have the power to take the action under this part. (b) A personal representative who has been granted authority to administer the estate under this part may give notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter even if the provision of Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 10500) giving the personal representative the power to take the action permits the personal representative to take the action without giving notice of proposed action."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10580 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10580(a)-(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10580.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes both subdivision (a) and subdivision (b) of the same statutory section, Probate Code § 10580, as a single continuous quotation — they are not independent sources of one another. Whether a given action requires notice under this chapter depends on the specific Chapter 3 provision (§§ 10500 et seq.) granting the power to take it; this document does not enumerate those individual provisions or state which of them require notice, which permit it optionally, and which require neither. Within the sections fetched and verified for this document (§§ 10580-10592 and Probate Code § 1215), no separate expedited, shortened, or emergency-notice procedure for urgent matters was found; this document does not represent that no such procedure exists anywhere else in the Probate Code, only that none appears in the sections checked here.

WHO MUST BE GIVEN NOTICE, AND HOW WRITTEN CONSENT OR A WRITTEN WAIVER ELIMINATES THAT REQUIREMENT
Probate Code § 10581 identifies who must be given notice of a proposed action regarding Pat Morgan's estate: each known devisee and each known heir whose interest in the estate would be affected by the proposed action, each person who has filed a request for special notice of petitions in the proceeding, and the Attorney General (at the Attorney General's Sacramento office) if any part of the estate would escheat to the state and the state's interest would be affected. Two statutes let that notice obligation be eliminated for a particular person. Probate Code § 10582 provides that notice need not be given to a person who consents in writing to the proposed action, and that consent may be signed before or after the action is taken. Probate Code § 10583(a) provides that notice need not be given to a person who, in writing, waives the right to notice of proposed action for that particular proposed action — a waiver that may likewise be signed before or after the action is taken, may describe the particular action, and may waive only particular aspects of notice (such as the delivery, mailing, or time requirements) or the giving of notice for that action in its entirety; § 10583(b) also recognizes a Judicial-Council-form Statutory Waiver that can be either a general waiver of notice or a waiver as to an entire category of transactions. Probate Code § 10584 governs revoking a waiver or consent already given: revocation must be in writing and is effective only when the personal representative actually receives it; a copy may be, but need not be, filed with the court for the revocation to be effective.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Except as provided in Sections 10582 and 10583, notice of proposed action shall be given to all of the following: (a) Each known devisee whose interest in the estate would be affected by the proposed action. (b) Each known heir whose interest in the estate would be affected by the proposed action. (c) Each person who has filed a request under Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 1250) of Part 2, of Division 3 for special notice of petitions filed in the administration proceeding. (d) The Attorney General, at the office of the Attorney General in Sacramento, if any portion of the estate is to escheat to the state and its interest in the estate would be affected by the proposed action."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10581 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10581 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10581.)
  "Notice of proposed action need not be given to any person who consents in writing to the proposed action. The consent may be executed at any time before or after the proposed action is taken."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10582 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10582 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10582.)
  "(a) Notice of proposed action need not be given to any person who, in writing, waives the right to notice of proposed action with respect to the particular proposed action. The waiver may be executed at any time before or after the proposed action is taken."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10583(a) (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10583(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10583.)
  "(a) A waiver or consent may be revoked only in writing and is effective only when the writing is received by the personal representative. (b) A copy of the revocation may be filed with the court, but the effectiveness of the revocation is not dependent upon a copy being filed with the court."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10584 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10584 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10584.)
  Known gap: This clause cites four separately numbered statutory sections — §§ 10581, 10582, 10583, and 10584 — each quoted once; none of the four citations is a subsection of another cited section, so they are independent of one another. Section 10583(b)'s reference to the Judicial Council's prescribed Statutory Waiver of Notice of Proposed Action form is described here only as the statute itself describes it; this document does not reproduce or link to that form.

WHAT THE NOTICE MUST SAY, AND HOW AND WHEN IT MUST BE DELIVERED
Probate Code § 10585(a) requires a notice of proposed action to state: the personal representative's name, mailing address, and electronic address; the name, telephone number, and electronic address of a person who can be contacted for more information; the proposed action itself, described in reasonably specific terms (with additional required detail — the material transaction terms, including sale price and any commission or compensation arrangement — if the action involves the sale or exchange of real property or granting an option to purchase real property); and the date on or after which the action is to be taken. The notice may use the current Judicial Council form, or a substantially similar form that contains the § 10585(a) statements and an objection form substantially like the Judicial Council's. Probate Code § 10586 requires the notice to be delivered, under Probate Code § 1215, to each person entitled to it not less than 15 days before the date stated in the notice as the date on or after which the action will be taken, and requires that a mailed notice be addressed to the person's last known address. Section 1215 itself sets out three delivery methods available for this notice (absent a different rule specific to the notice): delivery by mail (first-class mail within the United States, international mail otherwise), which is complete when deposited in the mail; personal delivery, complete when the notice is handed to the recipient; and electronic delivery, available only where the recipient has expressly consented on the appropriate Judicial Council form and supplied an electronic address for that purpose, complete when the notice is sent. Section 1215 states expressly that, for both mailed and electronic delivery, the period of notice is not extended — the 15-day period under § 10586 runs the same way regardless of which of these delivery methods is used.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) The notice of proposed action shall state all of the following: (1) The name, mailing address, and electronic address of the personal representative. (2) The name, telephone number, and electronic address of a person who may be contacted for additional information. (3) The action proposed to be taken, with a reasonably specific description of the action. If the proposed action involves the sale or exchange of real property, or the granting of an option to purchase real property, the notice of proposed action shall state the material terms of the transaction, including, if applicable, the sale price and the amount of, or method of calculating, any commission or compensation paid or to be paid to an agent or broker in connection with the transaction. (4) The date on or after which the proposed action is to be taken."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10585 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10585(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10585.)
  "The notice of proposed action shall be delivered pursuant to Section 1215 to each person required to be given notice of proposed action not less than 15 days before the date specified in the notice of proposed action on or after which the proposed action is to be taken. If mailed, the notice of proposed action shall be addressed to the person at the person’s last known address."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10586 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10586 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10586.)
  "(a) Delivery by mail. (1) A notice or other paper shall be delivered by mail as follows: (A) By first-class mail if the person’s address is within the United States. First-class mail includes certified, registered, and express mail. (B) By international mail if the person’s address is not within the United States. International mail includes first-class mail international, priority mail international, priority mail express international, and global express guaranteed. (2) The notice or other paper shall be deposited for collection in the United States mail, in a sealed envelope, with postage paid, addressed to the person to whom it is mailed. (3) Subject to Section 1212, the notice or other paper shall be addressed to the person at the person’s place of business or place of residence. (4) Delivery by mail is complete when the notice or other paper is deposited in the mail. The period of notice is not extended. (b) Personal delivery. (1) A notice or other paper may be delivered personally to that person. (2) Personal delivery is complete when the notice or other paper is delivered personally to the person who is to receive it. (c) Electronic delivery. (1) A notice or other paper shall not be delivered by electronic means unless the person to receive notice has expressly consented on the appropriate Judicial Council form to receive electronic delivery in the proceeding before the court and has provided an electronic address for that express purpose. (2) Electronic delivery is complete when the notice or other paper is sent. The period of notice is not extended."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 1215 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 1215(a)-(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=1215.)
  Known gap: This clause cites three separately numbered, independently sourced statutes: Probate Code §§ 10585 and 10586 (Division 7, Part 6, Chapter 4 — the notice-of-proposed-action chapter itself) and Probate Code § 1215 (Division 3, Part 2, Chapter 2 — the Probate Code's general mailing-and-delivery statute, in an entirely different division of the code). None is a subsection of another cited section here, so all three are independent of one another. Section 1215(a)(3) also cross-references Probate Code § 1212 regarding the address to which a mailed notice must be sent; this document does not independently verify or quote § 1212. This clause does not reproduce the Judicial Council's prescribed Notice of Proposed Action form referenced in § 10585(b)-(c).

HOW A PERSON OBJECTS TO A PROPOSED ACTION, AND THE RESTRAINING-ORDER ALTERNATIVE
Probate Code § 10587(a) gives any person entitled to notice of a proposed action under § 10581 the right to object to it. Under § 10587(b), the objection is made by delivering — under Probate Code § 1215 — a written objection to the personal representative at the address stated in the notice, either using the Judicial Council form or any other writing that identifies the proposed action with reasonable certainty and states that the person objects to it. Section 10587(c) provides that the personal representative is deemed to have notice of the objection if it is delivered or received at that address before whichever is later: the date stated in the notice as the date on or after which the action is to be taken, or the date the action is actually taken. Separately, Probate Code § 10588(a) lets any person entitled to notice apply to the court for an order restraining the personal representative from taking the proposed action without court supervision, and requires the court to grant that order without notice to the personal representative and without the applicant having to show cause.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) Any person entitled to notice of proposed action under Section 10581 may object to the proposed action as provided in this section. (b) The objection to the proposed action is made by delivering pursuant to Section 1215 a written objection to the proposed action to the personal representative at the address stated in the notice of proposed action. The person objecting to the proposed action either may use the Judicial Council form or may make the objection in any other writing that identifies the proposed action with reasonable certainty and indicates that the person objects to the taking of the proposed action. (c) The personal representative is deemed to have notice of the objection to the proposed action if it is delivered or received at the address stated in the notice of proposed action before whichever of the following times is the later: (1) The date specified in the notice of proposed action on or after which the proposed action is to be taken. (2) The date the proposed action is actually taken."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10587 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10587 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10587.)
  "(a) Any person who is entitled to notice of proposed action for a proposed action described in subdivision (a) of Section 10580, or any person who is given notice of a proposed action described in subdivision (b) of Section 10580, may apply to the court having jurisdiction over the proceeding for an order restraining the personal representative from taking the proposed action without court supervision. The court shall grant the requested order without requiring notice to the personal representative and without cause being shown for the order."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10588(a) (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10588(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10588.)
  Known gap: This clause cites two separately numbered sections, §§ 10587 and 10588, each quoted once; neither citation is a subsection of the other. Probate Code § 10588(b), which addresses how and when a personal representative is deemed to have notice of a restraining order (including a cross-reference to Code of Civil Procedure §§ 415.10 and 415.30 for the manner of service), was reviewed but is not quoted or independently verified against those Code of Civil Procedure sections here, so this clause omits its specific terms rather than characterize them without that verification.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER A TIMELY OBJECTION — AND WHAT HAPPENS IF NO ONE OBJECTS
Probate Code § 10589 states what a personal representative must do once notified of a timely objection or restraining order. Under § 10589(a), if the proposed action is one that would have required court supervision had the personal representative not held IAEA authority, and the personal representative has notice of a written objection under § 10587 or a restraining order under § 10588, the personal representative may take that action — if still desired — only under the Probate Code's ordinary court-supervision provisions for that kind of action; the notice-of-proposed-action procedure itself does not authorize taking it. Under § 10589(b), if the proposed action is one that would not have required court supervision even without IAEA authority, but the personal representative chose to give notice anyway and then received a timely objection or restraining order, the personal representative must request instructions from the court and may take the action only under whatever order the court enters. On the other side, Probate Code § 10590(a) addresses what happens when no one objects: except in narrow circumstances described elsewhere in that section, a person described in § 10581 who has been given notice under §§ 10580 through 10586 and does not object within the time and manner § 10587 provides waives the right to have a court review the action, or to object to it, after it has been taken; the same waiver applies to a person who has consented to or waived notice of the action under §§ 10582 through 10584.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) If the proposed action is one that would require court supervision if the personal representative had not been granted authority to administer the estate under this part and the personal representative has notice of a written objection made under Section 10587 to the proposed action or a restraining order issued under Section 10588, the personal representative shall, if the personal representative desires to take the proposed action, take the proposed action under the provisions of this code dealing with court supervision of that kind of action. (b) If the proposed action is one that would not require court supervision even if the personal representative had not been granted authority to administer the estate under this part but the personal representative has given notice of the proposed action and has notice of a written objection made under Section 10587 to the proposed action or a restraining order issued under Section 10588, the personal representative shall, if he or she desires to take the proposed action, request instructions from the court concerning the proposed action. The personal representative may take the proposed action only under such order as may be entered by the court."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10589 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10589(a)-(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10589.)
  "(a) Except as provided in subdivision (c), only a person described in Section 10581 has a right to have the court review the proposed action after it has been taken or otherwise to object to the proposed action after it has been taken. Except as provided in subdivisions (b) and (c), a person described in Section 10581 waives the right to have the court review the proposed action after it has been taken, or otherwise to object to the proposed action after it has been taken, if either of the following circumstances exists: (1) The person has been given notice of a proposed action, as provided in Sections 10580 to 10586, inclusive, and fails to object as provided in subdivision (d). (2) The person has waived notice of or consented to the proposed action as provided in Sections 10582 to 10584, inclusive."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10590(a) (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10590(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10590.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Probate Code § 10589 (subdivisions (a) and (b), as one continuous quotation — not independent of one another) and Probate Code § 10590, subdivision (a) only, as a second, independent citation. Section 10590 contains further subdivisions — (b) and (c) — that create narrow exceptions to the waiver described here (for a person who establishes actual non-receipt of the notice before the objection period ran, and for an heir or devisee who lacked capacity or was a minor at the time notice was given, under further conditions involving that person's guardian, conservator, or other legal representative) and a subdivision (d) defining how an objection is made for purposes of that section; this clause does not quote or independently verify those additional subdivisions and does not purport to state them.

CONSEQUENCES IF THE PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVE DOES NOT FOLLOW THE NOTICE PROCEDURE
Two statutes address what follows if a personal representative fails to comply with the notice-of-proposed-action procedure. Probate Code § 10591(a) provides that the personal representative's failure to comply with § 10580(a) and with §§ 10581, 10585, 10586, and 10589 — and taking the action without that compliance — does not itself affect the validity of the action taken, or the title of a bona fide purchaser to property conveyed or transferred, or the rights of a third person who dealt in good faith with the personal representative and changed position in reliance on the action without actual notice of the noncompliance; § 10591(b) adds that a person dealing with the personal representative has no duty to inquire or investigate whether the personal representative complied with those provisions. Separately, Probate Code § 10592 addresses the personal representative's own exposure for noncompliance: under § 10592(a), where notice of proposed action is required by this chapter, the court has discretion to remove the personal representative from office unless the personal representative gives the required notice, obtains a waiver of it, or obtains consent to the action, as the chapter provides; under § 10592(b), the court also has discretion to remove the personal representative for taking a proposed action in violation of § 10589 — that is, proceeding despite a timely objection or restraining order without the court supervision or instructions § 10589 requires.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) The failure of the personal representative to comply with subdivision (a) of Section 10580 and with Sections 10581, 10585, 10586, and 10589, and the taking of the action by the personal representative without such compliance, does not affect the validity of the action so taken or the title to any property conveyed or transferred to bona fide purchasers or the rights of third persons who, dealing in good faith with the personal representative, changed their position in reliance upon the action, conveyance, or transfer without actual notice of the failure of the personal representative to comply with those provisions. (b) No person dealing with the personal representative has any duty to inquire or investigate whether or not the personal representative has complied with the provisions listed in subdivision (a)."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10591 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10591 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10591.)
  "(a) In a case where notice of proposed action is required by this chapter, the court in its discretion may remove the personal representative from office unless the personal representative does one of the following: (1) Gives notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter. (2) Obtains a waiver of notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter. (3) Obtains a consent to the proposed action as provided in this chapter. (b) The court in its discretion may remove the personal representative from office if the personal representative takes a proposed action in violation of Section 10589."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 10592 (California Legislative Information text), Prob. C. § 10592 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=10592.)
  Known gap: This clause cites two separately numbered sections, §§ 10591 and 10592, each quoted once in full; neither citation is a subsection of the other. Both provisions describe removal or protection as matters within the court's discretion ("may") rather than automatic consequences, and this clause does not characterize either outcome as guaranteed to occur in any particular case.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT — NOTICE OF PROPOSED ACTION PROCEDURE REFERENCE
I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that I have reviewed the foregoing information about the notice-of-proposed-action procedure in connection with the estate of Pat Morgan.

Executed on September 1, 2026 at Oakland, California.

Signature of Morgan Lee: ☐ _________________________

[This reference describes California's statutory notice-of-proposed-action procedure under Probate Code §§ 10580-10592. It does not itself give, waive, consent to, or object to notice of any proposed action, and it is not a substitute for an actual Notice of Proposed Action, written consent, written waiver, written objection, or court filing prepared and delivered in accordance with that procedure.]

Probate Code § 10586 requires the notice to be delivered, under Probate Code § 1215, to each person entitled to it not less than 15 days before the date stated in the notice as the date on or after which the action will be taken, and requires that a mailed notice be addressed to the person's last known address. Section 1215 itself sets out three delivery methods available for this notice (absent a different rule specific to the notice): delivery by mail (first-class mail within the United States, international mail otherwise), which is complete when deposited in the mail; personal delivery, complete when the notice is handed to the recipient; and electronic delivery, available only where the recipient has expressly consented on the appropriate Judicial Council form and supplied an electronic address for that purpose, complete when the notice is sent. Section 1215 states expressly that, for both mailed and electronic delivery, the period of notice is not extended — the 15-day period under § 10586 runs the same way regardless of which of these delivery methods is used.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10585 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) The notice of proposed action shall state all of the following: (1) The name, mailing address, and electronic address of the personal representative. (2) The name, telephone number, and electronic address of a person who may be contacted for additional information. (3) The action proposed to be taken, with a reasonably specific description of the action. If the proposed action involves the sale or exchange of real property, or the granting of an option to purchase real property, the notice of proposed action shall state the material terms of the transaction, including, if applicable, the sale price and the amount of, or method of calculating, any commission or compensation paid or to be paid to an agent or broker in connection with the transaction. (4) The date on or after which the proposed action is to be taken.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10586 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: The notice of proposed action shall be delivered pursuant to Section 1215 to each person required to be given notice of proposed action not less than 15 days before the date specified in the notice of proposed action on or after which the proposed action is to be taken. If mailed, the notice of proposed action shall be addressed to the person at the person’s last known address.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 1215 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) Delivery by mail. (1) A notice or other paper shall be delivered by mail as follows: (A) By first-class mail if the person’s address is within the United States. First-class mail includes certified, registered, and express mail. (B) By international mail if the person’s address is not within the United States. International mail includes first-class mail international, priority mail international, priority mail express international, and global express guaranteed. (2) The notice or other paper shall be deposited for collection in the United States mail, in a sealed envelope, with postage paid, addressed to the person to whom it is mailed. (3) Subject to Section 1212, the notice or other paper shall be addressed to the person at the person’s place of business or place of residence. (4) Delivery by mail is complete when the notice or other paper is deposited in the mail. The period of notice is not extended. (b) Personal delivery. (1) A notice or other paper may be delivered personally to that person. (2) Personal delivery is complete when the notice or other paper is delivered personally to the person who is to receive it. (c) Electronic delivery. (1) A notice or other paper shall not be delivered by electronic means unless the person to receive notice has expressly consented on the appropriate Judicial Council form to receive electronic delivery in the proceeding before the court and has provided an electronic address for that express purpose. (2) Electronic delivery is complete when the notice or other paper is sent. The period of notice is not extended.

None is a subsection of another cited section here, so all three are independent of one another. Section 1215(a)(3) also cross-references Probate Code § 1212 regarding the address to which a mailed notice must be sent; this document does not independently verify or quote § 1212. This clause does not reproduce the Judicial Council's prescribed Notice of Proposed Action form referenced in § 10585(b)-(c).

expectedJSON.body: Probate Code § 10587(a) gives any person entitled to notice of a proposed action under § 10581 the right to object to it. Under § 10587(b), the objection is made by delivering — under Probate Code § 1215 — a written objection to the personal representative at the address stated in the notice, either using the Judicial Council form or any other writing that identifies the proposed action with reasonable certainty and states that the person objects to it. Section 10587(c) provides that the personal representative is deemed to have notice of the objection if it is delivered or received at that address before whichever is later: the date stated in the notice as the date on or after which the action is to be taken, or the date the action is actually taken. Separately, Probate Code § 10588(a) lets any person entitled to notice apply to the court for an order restraining the personal representative from taking the proposed action without court supervision, and requires the court to grant that order without notice to the personal representative and without the applicant having to show cause.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10587 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) Any person entitled to notice of proposed action under Section 10581 may object to the proposed action as provided in this section. (b) The objection to the proposed action is made by delivering pursuant to Section 1215 a written objection to the proposed action to the personal representative at the address stated in the notice of proposed action. The person objecting to the proposed action either may use the Judicial Council form or may make the objection in any other writing that identifies the proposed action with reasonable certainty and indicates that the person objects to the taking of the proposed action. (c) The personal representative is deemed to have notice of the objection to the proposed action if it is delivered or received at the address stated in the notice of proposed action before whichever of the following times is the later: (1) The date specified in the notice of proposed action on or after which the proposed action is to be taken. (2) The date the proposed action is actually taken.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10588(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) Any person who is entitled to notice of proposed action for a proposed action described in subdivision (a) of Section 10580, or any person who is given notice of a proposed action described in subdivision (b) of Section 10580, may apply to the court having jurisdiction over the proceeding for an order restraining the personal representative from taking the proposed action without court supervision. The court shall grant the requested order without requiring notice to the personal representative and without cause being shown for the order.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause cites two separately numbered sections, §§ 10587 and 10588, each quoted once; neither citation is a subsection of the other. Probate Code § 10588(b), which addresses how and when a personal representative is deemed to have notice of a restraining order (including a cross-reference to Code of Civil Procedure §§ 415.10 and 415.30 for the manner of service), was reviewed but is not quoted or independently verified against those Code of Civil Procedure sections here, so this clause omits its specific terms rather than characterize them without that verification.

expectedJSON.body: Probate Code § 10589 states what a personal representative must do once notified of a timely objection or restraining order. Under § 10589(a), if the proposed action is one that would have required court supervision had the personal representative not held IAEA authority, and the personal representative has notice of a written objection under § 10587 or a restraining order under § 10588, the personal representative may take that action — if still desired — only under the Probate Code's ordinary court-supervision provisions for that kind of action; the notice-of-proposed-action procedure itself does not authorize taking it. Under § 10589(b), if the proposed action is one that would not have required court supervision even without IAEA authority, but the personal representative chose to give notice anyway and then received a timely objection or restraining order, the personal representative must request instructions from the court and may take the action only under whatever order the court enters. On the other side, Probate Code § 10590(a) addresses what happens when no one objects: except in narrow circumstances described elsewhere in that section, a person described in § 10581 who has been given notice under §§ 10580 through 10586 and does not object within the time and manner § 10587 provides waives the right to have a court review the action, or to object to it, after it has been taken; the same waiver applies to a person who has consented to or waived notice of the action under §§ 10582 through 10584.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10589 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) If the proposed action is one that would require court supervision if the personal representative had not been granted authority to administer the estate under this part and the personal representative has notice of a written objection made under Section 10587 to the proposed action or a restraining order issued under Section 10588, the personal representative shall, if the personal representative desires to take the proposed action, take the proposed action under the provisions of this code dealing with court supervision of that kind of action. (b) If the proposed action is one that would not require court supervision even if the personal representative had not been granted authority to administer the estate under this part but the personal representative has given notice of the proposed action and has notice of a written objection made under Section 10587 to the proposed action or a restraining order issued under Section 10588, the personal representative shall, if he or she desires to take the proposed action, request instructions from the court concerning the proposed action. The personal representative may take the proposed action only under such order as may be entered by the court.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10590(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) Except as provided in subdivision (c), only a person described in Section 10581 has a right to have the court review the proposed action after it has been taken or otherwise to object to the proposed action after it has been taken. Except as provided in subdivisions (b) and (c), a person described in Section 10581 waives the right to have the court review the proposed action after it has been taken, or otherwise to object to the proposed action after it has been taken, if either of the following circumstances exists: (1) The person has been given notice of a proposed action, as provided in Sections 10580 to 10586, inclusive, and fails to object as provided in subdivision (d). (2) The person has waived notice of or consented to the proposed action as provided in Sections 10582 to 10584, inclusive.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes Probate Code § 10589 (subdivisions (a) and (b), as one continuous quotation — not independent of one another) and Probate Code § 10590, subdivision (a) only, as a second, independent citation. Section 10590 contains further subdivisions — (b) and (c) — that create narrow exceptions to the waiver described here (for a person who establishes actual non-receipt of the notice before the objection period ran, and for an heir or devisee who lacked capacity or was a minor at the time notice was given, under further conditions involving that person's guardian, conservator, or other legal representative) and a subdivision (d) defining how an objection is made for purposes of that section; this clause does not quote or independently verify those additional subdivisions and does not purport to state them.

expectedJSON.body: Two statutes address what follows if a personal representative fails to comply with the notice-of-proposed-action procedure. Probate Code § 10591(a) provides that the personal representative's failure to comply with § 10580(a) and with §§ 10581, 10585, 10586, and 10589 — and taking the action without that compliance — does not itself affect the validity of the action taken, or the title of a bona fide purchaser to property conveyed or transferred, or the rights of a third person who dealt in good faith with the personal representative and changed position in reliance on the action without actual notice of the noncompliance; § 10591(b) adds that a person dealing with the personal representative has no duty to inquire or investigate whether the personal representative complied with those provisions. Separately, Probate Code § 10592 addresses the personal representative's own exposure for noncompliance: under § 10592(a), where notice of proposed action is required by this chapter, the court has discretion to remove the personal representative from office unless the personal representative gives the required notice, obtains a waiver of it, or obtains consent to the action, as the chapter provides; under § 10592(b), the court also has discretion to remove the personal representative for taking a proposed action in violation of § 10589 — that is, proceeding despite a timely objection or restraining order without the court supervision or instructions § 10589 requires.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10591 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) The failure of the personal representative to comply with subdivision (a) of Section 10580 and with Sections 10581, 10585, 10586, and 10589, and the taking of the action by the personal representative without such compliance, does not affect the validity of the action so taken or the title to any property conveyed or transferred to bona fide purchasers or the rights of third persons who, dealing in good faith with the personal representative, changed their position in reliance upon the action, conveyance, or transfer without actual notice of the failure of the personal representative to comply with those provisions. (b) No person dealing with the personal representative has any duty to inquire or investigate whether or not the personal representative has complied with the provisions listed in subdivision (a).

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 10592 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: (a) In a case where notice of proposed action is required by this chapter, the court in its discretion may remove the personal representative from office unless the personal representative does one of the following: (1) Gives notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter. (2) Obtains a waiver of notice of proposed action as provided in this chapter. (3) Obtains a consent to the proposed action as provided in this chapter. (b) The court in its discretion may remove the personal representative from office if the personal representative takes a proposed action in violation of Section 10589.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause cites two separately numbered sections, §§ 10591 and 10592, each quoted once in full; neither citation is a subsection of the other. Both provisions describe removal or protection as matters within the court's discretion ("may") rather than automatic consequences, and this clause does not characterize either outcome as guaranteed to occur in any particular case.
